description: NarrativeTrace for TypeScript records each traced call, its parameters and its result, forwards them as log lines through the pino or winston bridge, and writes a value-free structural trace per Vitest test. It installs from npm as @narrativetrace/core-node and @narrativetrace/proxy, with @narrativetrace/vitest for tests.
rules: Install with `npx @narrativetrace/cli init --dry-run`, read the diff, then run it without the flag; it copies agent skills into .agents/skills and .claude/skills and adds a marked section to AGENTS.md.
Choose one integration per project, as documentation/choosing-an-integration.md says: @narrativetrace/vitest, @narrativetrace/proxy, express, hono, nestjs, angular or react.
Values matching the redaction rules are replaced with [REDACTED] before any output. Keep secrets out of traced parameters and prove redaction with a test that traces a deny-listed parameter.
Only wrapped code appears in a trace: pass objects through traceObject and name parameters explicitly. Read the run's actual output before describing what the application did.
documentation/llms.txt is the curated reference, and documentation/recipes/ holds complete worked examples by problem.
